Review every anonymous sample against its supplied app-authored reading guide and brief. Inspect naturalness, grammar, lexical/grammatical load, clear references, narrative continuity and unresolved endings, contextual English definitions, missing useful definitions, redundant notes and Japanese readings when present. Scores 1–5: 1 severe mismatch, 2 material problems, 3 usable with reservations, 4 good, 5 unusually strong. samples.guide: Common concrete words, basic particles, simple polite or plain forms and clear short clauses. Canonical text omits readings. Provide contextual kana readings separately. No romaji.
samples.brief: Two friends at a railway station discover their tickets are for different destinations.

content.title: 二人の切符
content.story:
土曜日の朝、ゆいとけんは駅にいました。今日は一緒に海へ行きます。

ゆいは白いかばんを持っていました。かばんの中には、おにぎりとお茶がありました。けんはカメラを持っていました。

「海の写真をたくさん撮りたいです」とけんは言いました。
「私は海の近くでおにぎりを食べたいです」

二人は駅の時計を見ました。九時十分でした。

「電車は九時半ですね。切符を見ませんか」とゆいは言いました。

ゆいはかばんから切符を出しました。けんはポケットから切符を出しました。

「私の切符は青山駅までです」とゆいは言いました。
「えっ、僕の切符は青海駅までですよ」

二人は切符を並べました。ゆいの切符には「青山」、けんの切符には「青海」と書いてありました。

「本当ですね。違う駅ですね」

ゆいはもう一度、自分の切符を見ました。

「海へ行きたいです。でも、私の切符には『山』があります」

けんは駅の大きな地図を見ました。

「青海駅はここです。海の近くです。青山駅は……あ、ここです」

青山駅は山の近くにありました。海から遠い駅でした。

「名前が少し似ていますね」とゆいは言いました。「切符を買う時、間違えました」
「まだ時間がありますよ。駅の人に聞きませんか」

二人は窓口へ行きました。ゆいは駅の人に自分の切符を見せました。

「すみません。青海駅へ行きたいです。でも、この切符を買いました」

駅の人は切符を見ました。

「青山駅ですね。青海駅の切符に変えますか」
「はい、お願いします」

ゆいは新しい切符をもらいました。今度は「青海」と書いてありました。

「けんさん、今度は一緒ですね」
「はい。一緒に海へ行きましょう」

二人はホームへ歩きました。ホームには人がたくさんいました。小さい子どもが、お母さんと電車を待っていました。

ゆいは新しい切符をかばんに入れました。それから、駅の地図でもらった小さい紙を開きました。紙には海と山の絵がありました。

「青山駅の近くには、大きな公園があるんですね」

けんも紙を見ました。

「本当ですね。川もありますよ」
「今度は山へ行きませんか」
「いいですね。でも、今日は海ですよ」

二人は笑いました。

電車が来ました。ゆいとけんは電車に乗って、窓の近くに座りました。

けんはかばんからカメラを出しました。ゆいは海の絵を見ました。海のそばに、小さい島がありました。

「けんさん、この島へも行きたいです」

けんは窓の外から紙へ目を向けました。

「島ですか。船はありますか」

ゆいは紙の下を見ました。そこには船の絵と時間が書いてありました。

glossary.meaning: Saturday.
Morning.
Railway station.
To be present; used for people here. いました is polite past: were there.
Today.
Together; describes doing something with another person.
The sea; the friends' intended destination.
To go. 行きます is polite nonpast, 行きました is polite past, and 行きたいです expresses wanting to go.
Marks the direction or destination of movement, as in going to the sea.
Marks a location, recipient, or destination here, including being at the station and putting a ticket into a bag.
White; describes the bag.
Bag.
To hold or have with you. 持っていました describes having something with you at that time.
Inside; the interior of the bag.
Rice ball; food brought for the outing.
Tea.
To exist or be present; used for things and places. あります and ある are nonpast; ありました is polite past.
Camera.
Photograph; pictures Ken wants to take.
A lot; many photographs or many people.
To take a photograph. 撮りたいです means 'I want to take photographs.'
To say. 言いました is polite past.
I or me; Yui's self-reference. 私の means 'my.'
Nearby; the area close to something. の近く means 'near' the preceding place or object.
Marks where an action happens; here, eating near the sea.
To eat. 食べたいです means 'I want to eat.'
Two people; here, the two friends together.
Clock.
To look at or check something. 見ました is polite past.
Nine ten; 時 marks the hour and 分 marks minutes.
Polite sentence ending used to identify or describe something. でした is its past form.
Train.
Half past nine; 半 means half an hour in this time expression.
Sentence-ending particle inviting agreement or confirming a shared observation, like 'isn't it?'
Ticket; specifically a railway ticket here.
To look at or check something. 見ませんか politely suggests checking the tickets together.
From or out of; marks the source of something or a point from which distance is measured.
To take something out. 出しました is polite past.
Pocket.
As far as; marks the destination covered by a ticket.
A surprised 'What?' or 'Huh?' when Ken notices the destinations differ.
I or me; a self-reference commonly used by male speakers. Ken uses it here.
Sentence-ending particle emphasizing information for the listener, such as reassurance or a reminder.
To place things side by side. 並べました describes laying out the two tickets for comparison.
To be written on something. 書いてありました describes writing already present on the tickets or paper.
True; 本当ですね acknowledges that something really is the case.
To be different. 違う駅 means different stations.
Once more; again.
Oneself; 自分の切符 means one's own ticket, referring to Yui here.
But; introduces a contrast with what was just said.
Mountain; also the character Yui notices in the station name on her ticket.
Big or large; used directly before nouns such as map and park.
Map.
Here; this spot on the map.
Oh; signals noticing or finding something.
Far away; the station is far from the sea.
Name; here, the names of the stations.
A little; slightly.
To resemble or be similar. 似ています describes the station names being similar.
To buy. 買う is plain nonpast before 時; 買いました is polite past.
When; 買う時 means 'when buying' the ticket.
To make a mistake; here, choosing the wrong ticket. 間違えました is polite past.
Still; there is still time remaining.
Time; time available before departure, or a time shown on the paper.
Person or people. 駅の人 refers to a station staff member.
To ask. 聞きませんか politely suggests asking a station staff member.
Service counter or ticket window.
To show something to someone. 見せました is polite past.
Excuse me; a polite way to get the staff member's attention and introduce the problem.
This; used immediately before a noun, such as ticket or island.
To change or exchange something. 変えますか asks whether to exchange the ticket.
Yes; a polite affirmative response.
Please; politely accepts and requests the offered ticket exchange.
New; describes the replacement ticket.
To receive. もらいました is polite past; もらった is plain past modifying 紙, 'the paper received.'
This time; refers to the replacement ticket now having the correct destination.
Next time; refers to a possible future trip to the mountains.
The same; here, the friends now have matching destinations.
A polite suffix attached to someone's name when addressing them.
To go. 行きましょう politely proposes going together; 行きませんか politely invites someone to go.
Railway platform.
To walk. 歩きました is polite past.
Small; describes a child, paper, and island.
Child.
Mother; the child's mother here.
To wait for. 待っていました describes waiting for the train at that time.
To put something into something else. 入れました describes putting the ticket into the bag.
Then; after that. Connects successive actions.
Paper; the small sheet showing places and travel information.
To open or unfold something. 開きました describes opening the paper.
Picture or drawing; images on the paper.
Park.
So there is one; acknowledges newly discovered information with an explanatory tone.
Also or too; adds Ken, a river, or another destination to what has already been mentioned.
River.
Good or nice. いいですね expresses approval of the suggested trip.
To laugh or smile. 笑いました is polite past.
To come or arrive. 来ました describes the train arriving.
To board or ride a vehicle. 乗って is the linking form, joining boarding the train to the next action.
Window.
To sit down. 座りました is polite past.
Beside or near; the island is close to the sea in the picture.
Island.
Outside; the view outside the train window.
To turn one's eyes or attention toward something. 目を向けました describes Ken shifting his gaze to the paper.
Boat or ship; a possible way to reach the island.
Bottom or lower part; the lower section of the paper.
There; refers to the lower part of the paper just mentioned.
Marks the topic: what or whom the sentence is about. In には, it highlights a location or item being discussed.
Marks the subject or identifies what is present, such as tea, people, or a boat.
Marks the object of an action, such as a ticket being checked or a photograph being taken.
Connects nouns to show possession or a relationship, as in 'my ticket' or 'the station's clock.'
And or with; connects the two friends, lists things, or marks being with someone's mother.
Marks quoted speech or written content before verbs such as 'say' and 'be written.'
Sentence-ending question particle, used in questions and polite invitations.

materialIssues: 「駅の地図でもらった小さい紙」 unnaturally says the paper was received at or through the station map. Its acquisition was never narrated; 「駅の窓口でもらった小さい紙」 would establish a plausible source.
「海のそばに、小さい島がありました」 awkwardly places an island beside the sea rather than in it. If proximity to shore is intended, 「海岸の近くに」 would express that more clearly.

「と書いてありました」「もらった小さい紙」「あるんですね」「窓の外から紙へ目を向けました」 add result-state grammar, a past-form noun modifier, explanatory grammar, and a less transparent gaze expression. Their combined load stretches the supplied basic-short-clause guide, although the notes provide useful support.

「青山」「青海」「九時十分」 have no separate contextual kana readings. The canonical text correctly omits readings, but the required reading support is entirely absent; the station names particularly require author-selected pronunciations.
「でも」 has the forms list 「でも」「But」. The English translation is incorrectly included as a Japanese surface form.
strengths: The different-ticket discovery is clear, with concrete objects and mostly short, accessible clauses.
Definitions support common words, particles, contextual senses, and many actual inflected forms rather than merely supplying dictionary translations.
The separate explanations of 「今度」 accurately distinguish this time from next time.
The boat picture and timetable create a natural unresolved possibility after the ticket problem is resolved.
